Rashi on Eruvin 4b:10:1.english: A matter of Torah - A halakha given to Moses at Sinai, in the Oral Torah.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:10:2.hebrew: רובו - רוב שערו, שאם יש בו דבר החוצץ כגון דם יבש ודיו וטיט יבש וזפת יבש, או שקשור רובו אחת אחת:
Rashi on Eruvin 4b:10:2.english: Most of it - [I.e., most of his hair:] if there is in it a substance that serves as a barrier (chatzitz), such as dried blood, ink, dry clay, or dry pitch, or if most of it is tied up, each strand separately.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:10:3.english: And is particular about it - That is, he is distressed by this filth on his head.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:10:4.english: And that which he is not particular about - It is considered like his body, and even if it is the majority of it, it does not serve as a partition.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:10:5.hebrew: וגזרו על רובו שאינו מקפיד - הואיל והוי רוב, ודמי במקצת לחציצה דאורייתא:
Rashi on Eruvin 4b:10:5.english: And they decreed regarding the majority [of the interposing substance] that one is not particular about - Since it is a majority, and in some respects it resembles an interposition of Torah law:

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:10:6.hebrew: ועל מיעוטו המקפיד - הואיל ודמי ליה בהקפדה, וגזרו לאו הלכה למשה מסיני הוא, אלא גזירה מדרבנן, ורובו המקפיד לחודיה הוא דהוה הלכה למשה מסיני:
Rashi on Eruvin 4b:10:6.english: And on the minority of the one who is particular - Since it is similar to a case of [the owner] being particular, and [the Sages] decreed it, it is not a halakha from Moses at Sinai but a rabbinic decree. It is the majority of [cases of] one who is particular on his own that was a halakha from Moses at Sinai.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:11:1.english: And let [the Sages] also decree concerning the minority [of cases] in which one does not mind it, because of the minority in which one does mind it - They are alike to one another, this minority and that minority.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:11:2.hebrew: אי נמי - ניגזור בו משום רובו שאינו מקפיד, דדמי להדדי, דהאי אינו מקפיד והאי אינו מקפיד:
Rashi on Eruvin 4b:11:2.english: Alternatively - We should decree regarding it because of its majority, which is not particular, since they are alike: this one is not particular, and that one is not particular.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:12:1.english: It itself is a decree - because most of it is something one is particular about, as stated:

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:14:1.hebrew: ארון תשעה וכפורת טפח - ארון גובהו תשעה טפחים, דכתיב (שמות כ״ה:כ״ב) ואמה וחצי קומתו וכפורת טפח, הרי עשרה. וכתיב ודברתי אתך מעל הכפורת. ותניא בפ"ק דסוכה (ד' ה.) רבי יוסי אומר, לעולם לא ירדה שכינה למטה מעשרה, דכתיב השמים שמים לה' והארץ נתן לבני אדם. ולמטה מעשרה טפחים חשיב ארץ, דכתיב ודברתי אתך מעל הכפורת. אלמא עשרה הוי מחיצה, דלמעלה מעשרה לא חשיב ליה רשות תחתית, אלא רשותא אחריתי:
Rashi on Eruvin 4b:14:1.english: The ark, nine [tefachim], and the kapporet, a tefach - The height of the ark is nine tefachim, as it is written (Exodus 25:22): "and a cubit and a half is its height," and the kapporet is a tefach, which makes ten. And it is written: "And I will speak with you from above the kapporet." And it was taught in the first chapter of Sukkah (5a): Rabbi Yose says: The Divine Presence never descended lower than ten [tefachim], as it is written: "The heavens are the Lord's heavens, but the earth He gave to the children of men." Anything lower than ten tefachim is considered earth, as it is written: "And I will speak with you from above the kapporet." Thus it is evident that ten is a partition; anything above ten is not considered a lower domain, but a different domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:14:2.english: A handbreadth - Corresponding to the width of a beam and [the space] beneath it:

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:15:1.english: Walls of a structure - such as the walls of planks and curtains.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:15:2.english: Cubit of vessels - Such as the cubits of the ark, the altars, and the table.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:15:3.hebrew: באמה בת חמשה - דהשתא לא נפקא ליה מארון מידי, דלר' יהודה לא הוי לארון בהדי כפורת אלא שמנה טפחים ומחצה:
Rashi on Eruvin 4b:15:3.english: In an amah of five - Now [that the amah is five tefachim], nothing further results from the ark, since according to R. Yehuda the ark together with its cover amounts to only eight and a half tefachim.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:16:1.hebrew: בבינונית - באמה בת ו' בינונית לכל אדם, ויש גדולה ממנה כדאמר בכיצד צולין (פסחים פו.), שתי אמות היו בשושן הבירה, אחת יתירה על של משה חצי אצבע, ואחת יתירה עליה חצי אצבע, נמצאת. יתירה על של משה אצבע:
Rashi on Eruvin 4b:16:1.english: In the medium [amah] - The medium amah is six handbreadths for every person, but there is a larger one, as stated in (Pesachim 86a) in the chapter "Keitzad Tzolin": "There were two amot in Shushan the capital. One exceeded Moses' amah by half a finger, and the other exceeded that one by another half a finger, so that it exceeded Moses' amah by a full finger."

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:17:1.hebrew: לגוד - דאמרינן בכמה דוכתי, גוד אחית גוד אסיק, ופחות משלש כלבוד, ולשון לבוד כמו סניף, דבר קצר שהוסיפו עליו והאריכוהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 4b:17:1.english: To extend - As we say in many places: 'gud achit, gud asik' (extend it downward, extend it upward), and less than three [handbreadths] is like lavud. The term lavud is like snif, a short thing to which something was added and which was lengthened.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:18:1.english: And [one] comes to reduce it - By building a bench or heaping earth under the beam on the ground, to reduce the height of the open space beneath it.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:18:2.english: How much does he reduce? - Meaning: how much must one raise the ground?

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:18:3.english: How much it requires - Until the empty space is not more than twenty [cubits]:

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:19:1.english: Its width - This refers to the minimizing wall segment: how far must it be widened into the length of the alleyway?

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:19:2.english: A handbreadth - Corresponding to the width of a beam and its underside.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:1:1.hebrew: גרוגרת - היא תאנה יבישה ובה שיערו כל אוכל אדם לענין הוצאת שבת דתנן (שבת ד' עו:), המוציא אוכלין כגרוגרת: בעל הבית חס על כליו ואם ניקב כמוציא זית מצניעו לאגוזים כאגוז מצניעו לרמונים, לפיכך אם ניטמא וניקב עדיין טמא עד שינקב כמוציא רמון והיינו שיעורן כרמונים אבל כלי אומן העומד לימכר טהור בנקב קטן:
Rashi on Eruvin 4b:1:1.english: Grogeret - This is a dried fig, by which all people measured foodstuffs for carrying out on Shabbat, as we learned in the mishna (Shabbat 76b): One who carries out foodstuffs the size of a grogeret. A householder is protective of his vessels; if one is perforated to the size of an olive, he keeps it for nuts, and if it is perforated to the size of a nut, he keeps it for pomegranates. Therefore, if it became impure and was perforated, it remains impure until it is perforated to the size of a pomegranate, and this is their measure, as pomegranates. But a craftsman's vessel that is held for sale is pure with a small hole.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:20:1.hebrew: מאן דאמר טפח קסבר מותר להשתמש תחת הקורה - דאמר חודו החיצון יורד וסותם כדמשמע לקמן (עירובין ד' ח:), והלכך כיון דשיעור עשרים אמה משום היכר הוא, הרי יש היכר לעומד על אותו טפח שנגבה תחת הקורה:
Rashi on Eruvin 4b:20:1.english: Whoever says a handbreadth holds that one may use [the space] beneath the beam - That is, its outer edge descends and closes [the gap], as is implied later (Eruvin 8b). Therefore, since the twenty-cubit measure is only for the sake of demarcation, there is a demarcation for one standing on that handbreadth which is measured off beneath the beam.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:3:1.english: Most of its measures are olive-sized - Eating forbidden fat (chelev) and blood, [eating] notar, piggul, ritually impure food and carrion, an impure animal, corpse flesh (conveying impurity by overshadowing), and contact with carcasses. "Every 'honey' mentioned in the Torah is date honey, as it says there (Bikkurim 1:3): 'One may bring first-fruits only from the seven species, and not from the dates of the mountains or the fruits of the valleys.' Thus it is evident that the tanna takes it for granted that dates are among the seven species, namely honey."

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:6:1.hebrew: במים במי מקוה - המכונסין משמע, ואע"ג דלאו חיים מדלא כתיב חיים:
Rashi on Eruvin 4b:6:1.english: In water, in a mikveh - [The word "in water"] implies gathered water, even though it is not living water, since "living" is not written there.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:6:2.english: All his flesh - implying that all of his flesh [must be immersed] at once.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:7:1.english: To his hair - That a barrier would invalidate [the immersion] through it.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:7:2.english: And like Rabbah - For Rabbah said: a barrier invalidates [the immersion] in the hair.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:7:3.english: A single tied hair interposes - That it can be tied tightly, so that water does not enter the knot.

Rashi on Eruvin 4b:7:4.english: Three [things] do not interpose - Because they are not tightly packed, and water enters into them:

Tosafot on Eruvin 4b:10:1.hebrew: דבר תורה רובו ומקפיד עליו חוצץ - פי' בקונטרס בשערו משמע, אבל בשרו אפילו מיעוטו שאינו מקפיד חוצץ. וקשה לר"ת, דבפרק הערל (יבמות ד' עח. ושם) אמרינן: נכרית מעוברת שנתגיירה, אין בנה צריך טבילה. וקאמר: אילימא משום דר' יצחק? הא אמר רב כהנא: לא שנו אלא רובו, אבל כולו חוצץ! והשתא, אדרבה הוה ליה למימר: כי אמר ר' יצחק בשערו, בשרו מי אמר? ועוד, דבפ' דם חטאת (זבחים ד' צח.) מייתי: דם שעל בגדו חוצץ, ואם טבח הוא אינו חוצץ. ועוד: אי בשערו דווקא, אם כן כשנאמר הלכה למשה מסיני, הוצרך לומר שערו רובו ומקפיד עליו חוצץ; אם כן שערו הוי הלכה למשה מסיני, ואמאי צריך קרא לשערו? וכי האי גוונא פריך בכמה דוכתי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 4b:10:1.english: A matter of Torah law: if most of it [is present] and one is particular about it, it intervenes - Rashi explains that [the rule applies to] his hair, as is implied; but as for his flesh, even a minority of it, which one is not particular about, intervenes. And it is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam: in the chapter Ha-Erel (Yevamot 78a and there) we say that the child of a pregnant gentile woman who converted does not require immersion. And [the Gemara] says: "Shall we say it is because of R. Yitzchak? But Rav Kahana said: They taught [this] only regarding most of it, but if all of it [is present], it intervenes!" And now, on the contrary, [the Gemara] should have said: "When R. Yitzchak said 'his hair,' did he say 'his flesh'?" Furthermore, in the chapter Dam Chatat (Zevachim 98a) it cites: blood on one's garment intervenes, but if he is a butcher, it does not intervene. Furthermore: if [the rule] applies specifically to hair, then when it is stated as a halakha transmitted to Moses at Sinai, it would have been necessary to say "his hair, most of it, and one is particular about it, it intervenes"; so hair would be a halakha of Moses from Sinai, and why does it need a verse for his hair? And he raises such questions in many places.

Tosafot on Eruvin 4b:20:1.hebrew: מותר להשתמש תחת הקורה - פירש בקונטרס דקסבר חודו החיצון יורד וסותם, ומאן דאסר סבר חודו הפנימי יורד וסותם; ולא רצה לפרש, דמר סבר היכירא לבני רשות הרבים, ומר סבר היכירא לבני מבוי, משום דקאמר בתר הכי ואיבעית אימא, דכולי עלמא קורה משום היכירא, משמע דעד השתא לא הוי לכולי עלמא משום היכירא. ואין להקשות לפירושו, הואיל וסברי קורה משום מחיצה, א"כ, מאי טעמא דמאן דאמר טפח? והא לא הוי מחיצה לפחות מד', אין לחוש, הואיל והוי דופן, אלא שבא למעטו, כדפי' בקונטר' בענין זה בסמוך:
Tosafot on Eruvin 4b:20:1.english: Permitted to use beneath the beam - Rashi explained in the Kuntres that he holds the outer edge descends and closes off, while the one who prohibits holds the inner edge descends and closes off. And he did not wish to explain that one Master holds the heikeira is for those of the public domain and the other holds it is for those of the alley, because the Gemara says afterward, 'And if you wish, say that everyone holds the beam is for the sake of the heikeira', which implies that until now it was not, for everyone, for the sake of the heikeira. And one should not raise a difficulty against his explanation: since they hold the beam is for the sake of a barrier, then what is the reason of the one who says a tefach? For it is not a barrier if it is less than four [handbreadths]. There is no concern, since it is a side-wall (dofen), but it came to exclude it, as explained in the Kuntres on this matter below.

Tosafot on Eruvin 4b:2:1.hebrew: כל כלי בעלי בתים שיעורן כרמונים - גבי כלי עץ מתנייא במסכת כלים פרק י"ז (מ"א), אבל גבי כלי חרס תנן בפ"ג (מ"א), דכלים העשויים לאוכלים שיעורן כזית. והא דאמר בסוף המצניע (שבת ד' צה:) חמש מדות בכלי חרס ניקב כמוציא זית וכו', ועדיין כלי הוא לקבל בו רמונים; היינו היכא דייחדו לרמונים, אבל סתמא הוי כמוציא זית:
Tosafot on Eruvin 4b:2:1.english: All householders' vessels, whose measure is that of pomegranates - With regard to wooden vessels, this is taught in tractate Kelim, chapter 17 (Mishnah 1), but with regard to clay vessels we learned in chapter 3 (Mishnah 1) that vessels made for foodstuffs have the measure of an olive. As for what was said at the end of Ha-Matzni'a (Shabbat 95b): "Five measures [apply] to a clay vessel: if it is pierced like the emergence of an olive, etc., and it is still a vessel for receiving pomegranates." This applies where it was designated for pomegranates; but where it was not designated, it is [treated as] the emergence of an olive.

Tosafot on Eruvin 4b:2:2.hebrew: שיעורן כרמונים - בפרק י"ז במסכת כלים (מ"ד) תנן הרמונים שאמרו ג' אחוזים זה בזה, משמע דשיעורן בג' רמונים. וקשה, דבפרק המצניע (שבת ד' צה.) אמר: ניקב כמוציא רמון טהור, משמע רמון אחד. ולקמן פ"ב (עירובין ד' כד.) בעי חזקיה: ניקב כמוציא זית וסתמו וחזר וניקב עד שהשלימו למוציא רמון, מהו? ולא קאמר: ניקב כמוציא רמון וסתמו וחזר וניקב כמוציא רמון עד שהשלימו לג' רמונים, מהו? וי"ל, דג' אחוזים לא שיצאו ביחד אלא זה אחר זה, וצריך נקב רחב להוציא ג' בזה אחר זה יותר ממה שהיה האחד לבד. אי נמי, ג' אחוזים פירוש: שגדילים ג' ביחד, והם רמונים בינונים ולא מאותן שגדילין אחד או ב' יחד, שהם גדולים, ולא מאותן שגדילין ד' או ה' ביחד, שהם קטנים; ולעולם רמון אחד לבד קאמר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 4b:2:2.english: Their measure is like pomegranates - In chapter 17 of Kelim (mishnah 44) we learn: 'Pomegranates that were said to be three held one with another' - which implies that their measure is that of three pomegranates. And it is difficult: in chapter HaMatzni'a (Shabbat 95), [the Gemara] says: 'If a hole was made the size of removing a pure pomegranate,' which implies [the measure of] one pomegranate. And below, in chapter 2 (Eruvin 24), Hizkiyah asks: 'If a hole was made the size of removing an olive, and it was blocked, and then made again until it was enlarged to the size of removing a pomegranate, what is the law?' But he did not ask: 'If a hole was made the size of removing a pomegranate, and it was blocked, and then made again the size of removing a pomegranate, until it was enlarged to the size of three pomegranates, what is the law?' And one can answer: the three [pomegranates] did not come out together but one after another, and the hole must be wide enough to remove three one after another, more than would be needed for one alone. Alternatively, 'three held together' means three growing together, and these are medium-sized pomegranates - not those that grow one or two together, which are large, nor those that grow four or five together, which are small. And [the Mishnah] is always speaking of a single pomegranate on its own.

Tosafot on Eruvin 4b:5:1.hebrew: הילכתא נינהו ואסמכינהו רבנן אקראי - בפרק בתרא דיומא (ד' פ.) א"ר יוחנן שיעורין ועונשין הלכה למשה מסיני, והיה כתוב בספרים שיעורין מכתב כתיבי, אימא שיעורין של עונשין, ולא גרסי' הכי, דהא מסקינן הכא דאסמכתא נינהו, ועוד, דלא הוה משני מידי, אלא גרסינן עונשין מכתב כתיבי, אימא וכו':
Tosafot on Eruvin 4b:5:1.english: They are a halakha, and the Sages merely relied on a verse for them - In the last chapter of Yoma (folio 80), Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Measures (shi'urin) and penalties (onshin) are a halakha given to Moses at Sinai. And the texts had "shi'urin, mikhtav kitvei" (i.e., "measures [derived] from a written verse"); say instead "shi'urin shel onshin" (measures of penalties). But the text is not read that way, since we concluded here that they are an asmakhta, and moreover the Gemara would not have answered anything at all. Rather, we read "onshin, mikhtav kitvei; say," etc.
